title: Quasi-coherent positive-copy graded algebra and symmetric quotient
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal E$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of commutative unital $\mathcal O_S$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Define homogeneous sheaves $\mathcal B_0=\mathcal O_S$ and $\mathcal B_n=\mathcal E$ for $n\geq1$, writing $a[n]$ for a section in the degree-$n$ copy. Give their categorical sheaf direct sum the multiplication $a[m]b[n]=(ab)[m+n]$ for $m,n>0$, degree-zero action through $\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal E$, and unit in degree zero. These operations define a commutative unital graded sheaf algebra [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], and its underlying module is quasi-coherent. For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], putting $A=\mathcal E(V)$, there is a canonical graded $R$-algebra identification
$$\mathcal B(V)=R\oplus\bigoplus_{n\geq1}A[n],$$
with the indicated multiplication, compatible with inclusions of affine opens. The degree-one inclusion of $\mathcal E$ extends uniquely to a degree-preserving morphism of sheaf algebras
$$q:\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_S}(\mathcal E)\longrightarrow\mathcal B,$$
where the source is the quasi-coherent symmetric algebra [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] with symmetric-degree grading [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. The map $q$ is the identity in degree zero and is surjective in every degree. No finite-type, local-freeness, or injectivity hypothesis on the algebra structure map is imposed.

proof.text: On sections define the zero-zero product in O_X, mixed products through the structure ring homomorphism of E, and positive-positive products in E. Construct the bilinear maps using LinearMap.mul and composition with the algebra structure map. Check naturality by ring-hom multiplicativity and naturality of the structure map. Check associativity in the eight zero/positive cases, commutativity in the four cases, and both unit laws in the two cases. Apply the total-algebra theorem to these homogeneous operations; it supplies B, its coproduct cocone, and the multiplication and scalar equations.

source.place: Tag 01CF, section-symmetric-exterior: homogeneous operations on a sheaf direct sum; explicit case verification for this algebra written by Q146

proof.text: Every homogeneous piece is quasi-coherent: the unit module is free of rank one, and positive pieces are E. Reindex the coproduct by ULift ℕ in the scheme universe. Quasi-coherent coproduct closure and the unique comparison isomorphism imply that B is quasi-coherent. On an affine open, quasiCoherentModuleColimitEvaluation makes the evaluated coproduct a module colimit. Reindex back to ℕ and compare with ModuleCat.coproductCoconeIsColimit, whose point is the sectionwise direct sum. The resulting isomorphism sends each direct-sum generator to its evaluated sheaf inclusion by the colimit comparison identity, so its hom is exactly positiveCopySectionSum. Therefore this map is bijective.

proof.text: For each open U apply Mathlib Submodule.pow_induction_on_right' to the range of the generator map. A scalar in degree zero has its prescribed scalar lift; sums have sums of lifts; if x has a lift a in degree n and m=ι(b) is a generator, then x*m maps to i_n(a)i_1(b)=i_{n+1}(G.mul(a,b)). This proves the homogeneous membership clause on every open directly, without an affine symmetric-algebra comparison or a separate grading theorem.

source.place: Tag 00DM, algebra-section-tensor-algebra (homogeneous pieces spanned by products), and Tag 01CF, section-symmetric-exterior (symmetric-degree grading of the sheaf)

proof.text: In degree zero lift r by algebraMap(r). In degree one lift a by ι(a). Inductively, if s lifts a in degree n+1, then s*ι(1_E) belongs to the next submodule power and maps to i_{n+1}(a)i_1(1_E)=i_{n+2}(a), by the homogeneous product equation and a*1_E=a. Thus every degree is surjective even on sections. Any algebra-sheaf map satisfying all clauses satisfies the generator clause, so uniqueness follows from the core universal property.

lean.statement: theorem exists_positiveCopyGradedQuotient (X : Scheme.{u}) (E : X.CommAlgebraSheaf) [E.toModule.IsQuasicoherent] : ∃ (B : X.CommAlgebraSheaf) (i : ∀ n : ℕ, positiveCopyPiece E n ⟶ B.toModule) (G : GradedSheafAlgebra (positiveCopyPiece E)), Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk B.toModule i)) ∧ B.toModule.IsQuasicoherent ∧ G.unit = 𝟙 (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (r s : Γ(X, U)), HEq (G.mul 0 0 U r s) (r * s)) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (n : ℕ) (r : Γ(X, U)) (a : E.right.obj.obj (op U)), HEq (G.mul 0 (n + 1) U r a) (E.hom.hom.app (op U) r * a)) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (n : ℕ) (a : E.right.obj.obj (op U)) (r : Γ(X, U)), HEq (G.mul (n + 1) 0 U a r) (a * E.hom.hom.app (op U) r)) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (m n : ℕ) (a b : E.right.obj.obj (op U)), HEq (G.mul (m + 1) (n + 1) U a b) (a * b)) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (m n : ℕ) (a : (positiveCopyPiece E m).val.obj (op U)) (b : (positiveCopyPiece E n).val.obj (op U)), (i (m + n)).val.app (op U) (G.mul m n U a b) = (@id (B.right.obj.obj (op U)) ((i m).val.app (op U) a)) * (@id (B.right.obj.obj (op U)) ((i n).val.app (op U) b))) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (r : Γ(X, U)), (i 0).val.app (op U) r = B.hom.hom.app (op U) r) ∧ (∀ U : X.affineOpens, Function.Bijective (positiveCopySectionSum E B i U.1)) ∧ ∃! q : SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.algebra E.toModule ⟶ B, (∀ (U : X.Opens) (a : E.right.obj.obj (op U)), q.right.hom.app (op U) ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.inclusion E.toModule).val.app (op U) a) = (i 1).val.app (op U) a) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (n : ℕ) (s : SymmetricAlgebra Γ(X, U) (E.toModule.val.obj (op U))), s ∈ (SymmetricAlgebra.ι Γ(X, U) (E.toModule.val.obj (op U))).range ^ n → ∃ a : (positiveCopyPiece E n).val.obj (op U), q.right.hom.app (op U) (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.sectionMap E.toModule (op U) s) = (i n).val.app (op U) a) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (r : Γ(X, U)), q.right.hom.app (op U) ((SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.algebra E.toModule).hom.hom.app (op U) r) = (i 0).val.app (op U) r) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (n : ℕ) (a : (positiveCopyPiece E n).val.obj (op U)), ∃ s : SymmetricAlgebra Γ(X, U) (E.toModule.val.obj (op U)), s ∈ (SymmetricAlgebra.ι Γ(X, U) (E.toModule.val.obj (op U))).range ^ n ∧ q.right.hom.app (op U) (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.sectionMap E.toModule (op U) s) = (i n).val.app (op U) a)
